stories.headline: ARMY CALL READY FOR 500,000 MEN; War Department Has Universal Service Plan Worked Out and Waits on Congress. BACKED BY GENERAL STAFF Selective Conscription Scheme to be Submitted When War Resolution Passes. ARMY CALL READY FOR 500,000 MEN Careful Selection at First. Want 20,000 Skilled Men.
stories.summary: war resolution passed by U. S. Sen.

stories.headline: DEBATE LASTED 16 1/2 HOURS; One Hundred Speeches Were Made;-Miss Rankin, Sobbing, Votes No. ALL AMENDMENTS BEATEN Resolution Will Take Effect This Afternoon with the President's Signature. KITCHIN WITH PACIFISTS Accession of the Floor Leader Added Others to the Anti-War Faction. Miss Rankin Votes "No." The Early Morning Scenes. A Feast of Speeches. Levity Amid the Solemnity. Flood Opens the Discussion. Kitchin's Stand Surprises Leaders. Alabamians in a Rumpus. Why Wilson Must Sign Resolution. EBB AND FLOW OF DEBATE. Pacifists' Pleas, with Interruptions, Provide Chief Interest. Denounces Talk of Expediency. Cooper First to Oppose. Sensation Over Zimmermann Note. Rush to Hear Kitchin Talk. Cites Course Toward Britain. Why Not Forego Violation of Rights? Non-Partisan Plea by Cannon. Intimates Kitchin Should Resign. Only One Course, Says Mann. War for Human Rights, Gardner Says. Calls for "Vote" Futile.
stories.summary: naval, military, and industrial preparedness being rushed

stories.headline: SEEKS BOYS' ARMY FOR STATE FARMS; Agricultural Society Starts a School Census to Discover the Number Available. EXPECTS 5,000 FROM HERE Plans Laid to Make Work Congenial and to Give Credits as for Classroom Tasks. REDFIELD ISSUES APPEAL. Asks Commercial Bodies to Help Increase Crops. REDFIELD APPEALS FOR FOOD SUPPLY CALL FOR SEED STATISTICS. Pennsylvania Takes Steps to Organize Agricultural Army. GAINS IN FOOD PRICES. Commissioner Hartigan, However, Says the Supply Here Is Adequate. ROCKEFELLER LAND FOR FOOD Others Will Join Westchester Movement for National Defense. QUICK ACTION IN NORTHWEST. Minnesota, Dakotas, and Montana Increasing Farm Operations. GERMAN-AMERICANS BALK. Ohio Leader Holds Food Increase Would Help England. CORNER FOR JERSEY POTATOES If Present Efforts Succeed They May Retail at $20 a Barrel.
stories.summary: N. Y. S. Agricultural Soc. starts movement to recruit boys' farm army by taking school census; H. E. Cole explains plan for placing boys in congenial groups; Sec. Redfield appeals to commercial bodies to help increase crops

stories.headline: CONGRESS VOTES ON DRAFT BILL TODAY; BIG MAJORITIES FOR IT ARE CLAIMED; HOUSE REJECTS ROOSEVELT ARMY PLAN; HOUSE OPPOSITION WEAKENS Kahn Leads Final Rally For Measure and Is Joined by Mann. 170 TO 106 AGAINST COLONEL Miss Rankin and Mr. Longworth Among Advocates of His Volunteer Force. AGE LIMIT STILL IN DOUBT Senate Favors 19 to 26, and the House 21 to 40;-Other Details to be Adjusted. Miss Runkin for Roosevelt. No Stigma, Mr. Mann Says. Lincoln's Letter Read. Duty to the Republic. SENATORS ADVOCATE DRAFT. Tide of Debate Turns in Favor of Administration Bill. Would Conscript Big Incomes. Attacks Volunteer System. Wants Submarine Board.
stories.summary: Repr. Austin offers amendment to permit Col. Roosevelt to take division to France

rounds.blurb: Among the month's major headlines: ARMY CALL READY FOR 500,000 MEN; DEBATE LASTED 16 1/2 HOURS; SEEKS BOYS' ARMY FOR STATE FARMS.

stories.headline: BERTAUD MAY LOSE POST IN BELLANCA; ITS FLIGHT IN DOUBT; Levine Considers Ousting Him, Insists Hop Will Be Made With Chamberlin as Pilot. BYRD'S AIDE DECLINES JOB Bertaud Wants to Buy Plane--Thomas L. Hill Also Offers $30,000, but Is Refused. AMERICA IN LOAD TESTS Commander Nearly Ready as the Weather Still Holds Fliers -- Lindbergh Visits About City. BYRD'S PLANE, AMERICA, IN THE AIR AT ROOSEVELT FIELD YESTERDAY. BERTAUD MAY LOSE POST IN BELLANCA
stories.summary: Bertaud-Levine controversy continues; Bertaud may lose post in Bellanca; B Balchen refuses offer to pilot it; its flight in doubt; summary of dispute; Bertaud's statement as to prize money; he offers to buy plane; T L Hill announces offer of $30,000 for it, not accepted; Levine says Chamberlin will fly in any event; Comdr Byrd praises Bertaud's spirit

stories.headline: FATE OF ATLANTIC FLIERS IS UNKNOWN AFTER DAY OF WATCHING AND RUMORS; BELLANCA PLANS TO START TOMORROW; WHITE BIRD MUST BE DOWN Grave Anxiety Is Felt for Nungesser and Coli, Now Long Overdue. WEATHER BAD ON ROUTE But Airmen Here Hope They May Be Safe -- Many Reports of Them Prove False. PARIS FEARS THE WORST Realizing Failure After Early News of Success, It Prays Fliers May Be Rescued. Map of Nungesser's Route Across Atlantic and Prevailing Weather Conditions
stories.summary: Rumors of bad conditions as nothing is heard of Nungesser and Coli; map of their route and prevailing conditions; fog forces F de Pinedo to defer Boston-Phila flight

stories.headline: BULK OF I.R.T. STOCK IS HELD IN WALL ST., HEARING DISCLOSES; About 90 Per Cent. of It Is a "Stock Market Football," Untermyer Charges. DIRECTORS' HOLDINGS SMALL Hayden Stone, of Which Dahl Was Partner, Leads List of Voting Certificate Owners. MILLER WANTS 'FAIR VALUE' But B.M.T. Won't Insist on Replacement Cost in Case of Recapture, He Says at Opening of Inquiry. BULK OF I.R.T. STOCK IS HELD IN WALL ST.
stories.summary: Hayden, Stone & Co, of which he was formerly a partner, found to lead list of voting certificate holders in I R T

stories.headline: COMMONS APPROVES BREAK WITH SOVIET; REJECTS LABOR PLEA; Motion for Inquiry Fails by Vote of 367 to 118, Order for Rupture Being Substituted. CLYNES ASKS 'FAIR TRIAL' Chamberlain Replies Verdict Is Already Justified -- Lloyd George Questions Result. WHITE PAPER OFFERS PROOF Government's Record of Moscow Intrigues Discloses Reds Here and Orders Sent From London. COMMONS APPROVES BREAK WITH SOVIET
stories.summary: S in defense of rupture of diplomatic relations, in Commons

stories.headline: OMINOUS SIGN IN MADRID; Heavy Decline on the Bourse Is Deemed Significant, But Other Indications Are Encouraging. POWERS MORE SYMPATHETIC Spain Urged, It Is Said, to Grant an Immediate Armistice -- The Papal Nuncio May Take a Hand -- War Preparations.
stories.summary: MADRID,, 7 P.M. -- The report published in the Imparcial, that United States Minister Woodford was preparing to leave Madrid, is entirely without foundation.

stories.headline: WAR TO BE DECLARED; Resolution Approved at a White House Sunday Conference to Go to Congress To-day. NO DELAY EXPECTED IN EITHER HOUSE. Sampson's Fleet Vigilant and Active Off the Cuban Coast Blockading Ports and Capturing Prizes. Flying Squadron Still at Fort Monroe -- Hongkong Ships Sailing for the Philippines -- No News of the Spanish Fleet.
stories.summary: Spain's Designs Against United States Ships

stories.headline: FIRST WAR ORDERS; The Flying Squadron to Move Against the Spanish Flotilla and Fleet. WILL CAPTURE AND HOLD THE CANARIES. Capt. Sampson's Fleet Will Co-operate, Placing the Spaniards Between Two Fires. Blow to be Struck Within Forty-eight Hours -- The Coast of Spain Will Then Be Invested and Cuba Invaded.
FIVE VESSELS ALMOST READY.; Three Torpedo Boats, a Gunboat, and a Submarine Boat Almost Completed -- The Holland Boat.
stories.summary: Vessels--Mackenzie, McKea, Rowan, Princeton, and Plunger--Under Construction
